office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Republican Skyler Rude, in the seat since 2019, faces Democrat Derek Sarley, a Walla Walla school-board member since 2015. Rude has announced he will resign effective October 31 to join the Secretary of State's office but remains on the ballot; if he wins, a Republican appointee would serve the term.

candidates.summary: State Representative since 2019 and Assistant Minority Floor Leader focused on education and budget reform, who has announced his resignation effective October 31 while remaining on the ballot.
highlights: Announced resignation effective October 31 to become legislative director for the Secretary of State; a win would lead to an appointed Republican successor [S17]
Voted against the 2026 tax on income over $1 million and calls himself a strong opponent of it [S3][S8]
Supports zero-based budgeting, expenditure limits and rolling back new programs [S5][S15]
Opposes statewide rent control and favors permitting and building-code streamlining [S4]
Voted against ESHB 1296 and the 2025 clean fuels bill [S11][S12]

taxes.basis: Voted no on ESSB 6346 and on the 2025 B&O (ESHB 2081) and services excise (ESSB 5814) tax bills; website says he was a strong opponent of the income tax and opposes new taxes.

spending.basis: Supports zero-based budgeting and expenditure limits, calls new programs during a deficit inexcusable and would roll them back.

housing.basis: Opposes statewide rent control and new landlord-tenant rules, favors faster permitting and cheaper building codes; voted against the 2025 tenant housing-stability bill.

climate.basis: Criticizes fuel-related taxes and prioritizes affordable energy; voted against the 2025 clean fuels program bill.

experience.basis: Four House terms since 2019 and Assistant Minority Floor Leader after prior legislative staff work.

local-control.basis: Says local control is paramount in data-center siting and the Legislature should safeguard local decisions.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296, the 2025 amendments to the parents' rights law, on House passage and final passage; no statement on notification or opt-outs.

tech.basis: Frames data-center policy around facilitating siting and adding energy and transmission rather than more regulation.

candidates.summary: Walla Walla school-board member since 2015, past president of the state school directors' association and PR-firm executive, running on school funding, affordability and budget reform.
highlights: Calls Washington's tax code the second-most regressive in the nation and recent progressive revenue steps important [S2][S6]
Opposes the 2026 K-12 and childcare cuts and wants the state to rebuild its rainy-day fund [S6][S8]
Wants more homes built faster with fewer building barriers, and a review of certificate-of-need health rules [S3][S7]
Endorsed by the Washington State Labor Council, WEA, WSNA, Planned Parenthood Advocates and the area Democratic parties [S5]

taxes.basis: Calls the tax code regressive and the Legislature's recent taxes on capital gains and high incomes important steps, while warning of their volatility.

spending.basis: Opposes K-12 and childcare cuts but says Democrats expanded services beyond revenue and wants spending held below revenue to rebuild reserves.

housing.basis: Wants more homes built faster with fewer outdated barriers and says the state cannot subsidize its way out of scarcity.

healthcare.basis: Focuses on cost and supply within the current system (middlemen, certificate-of-need review) rather than coverage expansion.

tech.basis: Opposes special tax breaks for data centers and wants ratepayer protections and equal environmental and water rules, while cautioning against rules that block building.

experience.basis: Ten years on a school board but new to the Legislature; asks voters to choose 'someone different.'

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Advocates; no statement of his own on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.
